questions.prompt: Old age is rather talkative, although wisdom is greater.
questions.answer: Senectūs loquācior est, quamquam sapientia maior est.

questions.prompt: The very brave captive bore the punishment in silence.
questions.answer: Captīvus fortissimus poenam tacitus tulit.

questions.prompt: This omen seemed somewhat too dreadful to the frightened soldiers.
questions.answer: Hoc prōdigium mīlitibus territīs horribilius vīsum est.

questions.prompt: The town was more rich than brave.
questions.answer: Oppidum dītius quam fortius erat.

questions.prompt: The winter nights are rather long for the sleepless watchman.
questions.answer: Noctēs hībernae vigilī insomnī longiōrēs sunt.

questions.prompt: Speak as clearly as possible, so that all may understand.
questions.answer: Quam clārissimē loquere ut omnēs intellegant.

questions.prompt: The furious king was more cruel than just.
questions.answer: Rēx furibundus crūdēlior quam iūstior erat.

questions.prompt: A very faithful friend does not desert us in danger.
questions.answer: Amīcus fīdēlissimus in perīculō nōs nōn dēserit.

questions.prompt: That trouble was somewhat greater than we had expected.
questions.answer: Illa molestia maior fuit quam exspectāverāmus.

questions.prompt: March by as short a road as possible into the mountains.
questions.answer: Quam brevissimā viā in montēs contende.

questions.prompt: The very wise old man taught the boys many things.
questions.answer: Senex sapientissimus puerōs multa docuit.

questions.prompt: This wine is sweeter than that which you praised.
questions.answer: Hoc vīnum dulcius est quam id quod laudāvistī.

questions.prompt: Bring back as many captives as possible from the war.
questions.answer: Quam plūrimōs captīvōs ex bellō redūc.

questions.prompt: The leader's speech was rather too long for the weary troops.
questions.answer: Ōrātiō ducis mīlitibus fessīs longior fuit.

questions.prompt: A very manly courage shone in the young man's face.
questions.answer: Virtūs virīlissima in ōre iuvenis ēlūxit.

questions.prompt: The unexpected messenger delayed longer than was fitting.
questions.answer: Nūntius inexspectātus diūtius quam decēbat remorātus est.

questions.prompt: Build the wall as high as possible against the enemy.
questions.answer: Mūrum quam altissimum contrā hostēs exstrue.

questions.prompt: The shameless woman was more bold than beautiful.
questions.answer: Mulier impudīca audācior quam pulchrior erat.

questions.prompt: These bones seem older than the whole town.
questions.answer: Haec ossa tōtō oppidō antīquiōra vidēntur.

questions.prompt: Return home as quickly as possible, for danger threatens.
questions.answer: Quam celerrimē domum redī, nam perīculum imminet.

questions.prompt: The general was more cautious than bold, and so avoided the ambush.
questions.answer: Dux cautior quam audācior erat, itaque īnsidiās vītāvit.

questions.prompt: Send as many hostages as possible into the enemy's camp.
questions.answer: Quam plūrimōs obsidēs in castra hostium mitte.

questions.prompt: The very greatest fear seized the sleepless watchman at midnight.
questions.answer: Vel maximus timor vigilem media nocte occupāvit.

questions.prompt: This building seems somewhat too high for so small a town.
questions.answer: Hoc aedificium altius quam prō tam parvā urbe vidētur.

questions.prompt: Old age is rather greedy, although it possesses much.
questions.answer: Senectūs avārior est, quamquam multa possidet.

questions.prompt: The prudent leader chose the very safest road through the mountains.
questions.answer: Prūdēns dux tūtissimam viam per montēs dēlēgit.

questions.prompt: Gather as great forces as possible before winter comes.
questions.answer: Quam maximās cōpiās parā antequam hiems veniat.

questions.prompt: In the eyes of the gods the exile seemed more wretched than guilty.
questions.answer: Exsul superīs miserior quam nocentior vidēbātur.

questions.prompt: Among the Helvetii, Orgetorix was by far the noblest and the richest.
questions.answer: Apud Helvētiōs longē nōbilissimus fuit et dītissimus Orgetorīx.

questions.prompt: The things which are reported about the sea-hare are no less marvelous.
questions.answer: Nōn sunt minus mīra quae dē lepore marīnō trāduntur.

questions.prompt: These things indeed I am accustomed to pursue even among the Sabines, and daily I fill up the banquet of my neighbors, which we prolong with varied conversation as late into the night as we possibly can.
questions.answer: Quae quidem etiam in Sabīnīs persequī soleō, convīviumque vīcīnōrum cotīdiē compleō, quod ad multam noctem quam maximē possumus variō sermōne prōdūcimus.

questions.prompt: Lead out with you also all your followers; if not, then as many as possible — purge the city!
questions.answer: Ēdūc tēcum etiam omnēs tuōs: sī minus, quam plūrimōs — pūrgā urbem!

questions.prompt: I do not put it off to too long a time, in which every longing is soothed and in which even the sharpest griefs subside.
questions.answer: Nōn differō in longius tempus, quō dēsīderium omne mulcētur, quō etiam ācerrimī lūctūs residunt.

questions.prompt: Good character has this among its other traits: it is pleased with itself, it endures. Malice is fickle; it often changes, not into something better but into something else.
questions.answer: Hoc habent inter cētera bonī mōrēs: placent sibi, permanent. Levis est malitia; saepe mūtātur, nōn in melius sed in aliud.

questions.prompt: Its little stalks or unripe figs, as small as possible, are drunk in wine against scorpion stings.
questions.answer: Cauliculī aut grossī eius quam minūtissimae ad scorpiōnum ictūs ē vīnō bibuntur.
